correctness.rationale: For all parameter choices, the binary logarithmic derivation A satisfies A(G)=alpha G, A(P)=beta P and det(U,A,Z)=G. In characteristic prime to d, E=U+zZ, B=A+(z beta/d)Z, T=z^(d-1)U+PZ are logarithmic and det(E,B,T)=F. In characteristic p dividing d, Z, U, W=(P-z^d)A are logarithmic with det(Z,U,W)=F. The reducedness iff criterion uses H_z=-d z^(d-1) and, when p|d, the nonvanishing of a partial of P unless all weights are p-multiples. A self-contained Cramer-division argument for reduced F yields full spanning of D(F). F_z=0 and H_z=0 explain polar collapse and concurrent H tangents. A standard-library exact verifier checks 13 instances without substituting finite tests for the theorem.

value.rationale: For a known family of free plane curves, this is an exact all-characteristic classification of an intrinsic graded module, including a characteristic-divisibility phase transition and the precise nonreduced boundary. The wild basis contains a degree-zero Frobenius derivation and coexists with all smooth nonlinear-component tangents meeting an exterior point. This algebraic and projective-geometric change persists in infinite families (for every prime p, weights 1,p-1). It is a structural theorem, not a routine numerical sample or a restatement of complex freeness.
